question: Can a data-derived probability blend beat the best simple choice, without hardwiring the number, identities or weights of its components?
eligible: Use every model with aligned raw probabilities on all three training folds already available from the original, expanded, matched-finalist and default runs, the identical-budget reconstruction and the registered frozen-encoder and encoder-size screens. Candidate inclusion uses file availability only. None of the designated-validation predictions, scores or labels are inputs. This is an offline development study with known training folds.
simple: Choose the strongest single or equal-weight group of up to three models by primary-fold accuracy. A tie favors fewer members, then an opaque deterministic tie-break. Freeze before opening confirmation probabilities.
weighted: Learn nonnegative weights summing to one by minimizing training-held multiclass Brier loss with a weak quadratic pull to uniform of magnitude 1/sqrt(n). If necessary keep at most the three largest weights, then refit the weights on that subset. Freeze the weights on the primary partition. Count the optimization fits separately.
advance: Compare that exact weighted proposal to both the frozen best equal-or-single option and its own equal-weight version. To advance, require positive accuracy gain over the main reference on each of the two confirmations, pooled gain of at least 0.003 over that reference, and positive pooled gain over equal weighting of its own members. If passed, freeze both recipes and buy trials on the two unused grouped folds before considering integration. Otherwise end this mechanism without opening any course validation data. This experiment alone cannot claim a formal course score.
budget: Up to two local convex weight fits now and at most twelve classifier fits for conditional new confirmations. No API, official test or H2.
